evals.prompt: A customer orders 200 units of a refrigerated vaccine. The nearest authorised distribution centre has two in-stock batches of the product: Batch A expires in 3 months, Batch B expires in 11 months. Which batch does AURORA allocate and why?
evals.expected_output: AURORA selects Batch A (the earlier expiry) under FEFO, subject to the product's minimum remaining shelf-life requirement.
expectations: Applies FEFO (First Expired, First Out) to the batch selection
Selects Batch A, the batch with the earlier expiry date
Notes the selection is subject to the product's minimum remaining shelf-life requirement

evals.prompt: A purchase order arrives. The customer-authorisation check passes, but the product is subject to an import suspension in the destination country. What must happen before the order can proceed?
evals.expected_output: Both the customer-authorisation check and the regulatory/product check must pass; the affected product lines are held or rejected and the regulatory uncertainty is escalated.
expectations: States that BOTH the customer-authorisation check AND the regulatory/product check must pass before the order proceeds
Does not proceed on the customer-authorisation check alone
Escalates the regulatory uncertainty to the compliance team / a Compliance Officer, or places the affected lines on hold

evals.prompt: The carrier reports that a shipment has arrived at the hospital, but the receiving staff have not yet confirmed receipt and the temperature indicator shows a brief excursion. Can AURORA close the shipment as delivered?
evals.expected_output: No — AURORA does not close a shipment on the carrier's arrival report alone; it requires recipient confirmation and routes the shipment to a quality hold because of the temperature excursion.
expectations: States the shipment must NOT be closed as delivered on the carrier's arrival report alone
Requires recipient confirmation of receipt, authorisation, and documentation
Routes the shipment to a quality hold / excursion investigation and prevents delivery release until quality assurance decides

evals.prompt: A critical-priority order is missing required information and the customer has not responded after 72 hours. What does AURORA do with the order?
evals.expected_output: AURORA does not auto-close a critical order for an unanswered request; it escalates to the Incident Management Team.
expectations: Does NOT auto-close the order because of the unanswered information request
Escalates to the Incident Management Team because the order is critical priority
Distinguishes this from the non-critical case (which is marked customer-unresponsive and closed)
